questions.prompt: What is the main trade-off when a value is typed as any?
options: Operations are allowed with little type checking, so mistakes can escape compile-time detection.
The value is deeply immutable at runtime.
The value is automatically validated when JSON is parsed.
The value can only ever be null.
questions.answer_key: Operations are allowed with little type checking, so mistakes can escape compile-time detection.
questions.explanation: any opts out of much of TypeScript checking; unknown is safer for untrusted values.

options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with purpose and behavior and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with purpose and behavior and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Purpose and behavior”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “The any Type”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check loss of type safety, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume safer alternatives to any is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check loss of type safety, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Loss of type safety”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
